brief.use_case: Assess whether a home is safe for a walker user discharged after hip replacement
brief.guideline:
Home Safety Check: Stairs and Bathroom (paraphrased from the CDC STEADI "Check for Safety" brochure)

STAIRS AND STEPS
- Nothing should be left on the steps: pick up shoes, books, bags and anything else you could trip on.
- Any step that is broken, loose or uneven must be repaired.
- There should be a light over the staircase, with a switch you can reach at the top and at the bottom.
- Handrails should be firmly attached on both sides of the stairs and run the whole length of the stairway.
- Carpet on the stairs must be tight to every step; remove it or tack it down if it is loose or torn.

BATHROOM
- The floor of the tub or shower needs a non-slip mat or adhesive safety strips.
- Grab bars should be installed inside the tub or shower and beside the toilet to help you get in, out, up and down.
- Small bath rugs that slide or have curled edges should be removed, or replaced with rugs that have a non-skid backing.
- Keep a night light on so the path to the bathroom is visible at night.
- A raised toilet seat or a toilet safety frame makes it easier to sit and stand, especially after hip surgery.

row.name: Objects on stairs
row.visual_description: Shoes, books, bags, or other items left on stair treads.
detection_cues: small objects resting on step surfaces
row.post_op_modifier: A walker user cannot step around clutter safely on stairs post-op, sharply raising fall risk.
row.citation: Nothing should be left on the steps: pick up shoes, books, bags and anything else you could trip on.

row.name: Broken or uneven steps
row.visual_description: Cracked, chipped, sagging, or unevenly spaced stair treads/risers.
detection_cues: visible crack or gap in tread
recommended_fix: Repair or replace damaged steps before use
row.post_op_modifier: Uneven footing is especially dangerous for a walker user with limited hip flexion and weight-bearing precautions.
row.citation: Any step that is broken, loose or uneven must be repaired.

row.name: Poor or unreachable stair lighting
row.visual_description: No overhead light fixture illuminating the staircase, or light switch not visible/reachable near top or bottom step.
detection_cues: no visible light fixture above stairs
switch absent near stair entry points
recommended_fix: Add switches at top and bottom landings
row.post_op_modifier: Reduced visibility increases misstep risk for a walker user who cannot quickly correct balance.
row.citation: There should be a light over the staircase, with a switch you can reach at the top and at the bottom.

row.name: Handrail missing on one or both sides
row.visual_description: Only one side of the staircase has a handrail, or no handrail is present at all, or rail does not span the full stairway length.
detection_cues: bare wall on one side of stairs
no rail visible on either side
recommended_fix: Install continuous handrails on both sides for full stair length
row.post_op_modifier: Bilateral support is critical for a walker user relying on handrails to offload the operative hip.
row.citation: Handrails should be firmly attached on both sides of the stairs and run the whole length of the stairway.

row.name: Handrail loose or not graspable
row.visual_description: Handrail wobbles, is detached from brackets, or is too thin/decorative to grip firmly.
detection_cues: visible gap between rail and wall bracket
rail material too slim for a full grip
recommended_fix: Re-secure or replace handrail with a firmly anchored, graspable rail
row.post_op_modifier: A loose rail can give way exactly when a walker user leans on it for stability, risking a fall onto the surgical hip.
row.citation: Handrails should be firmly attached on both sides of the stairs and run the whole length of the stairway.

row.name: Loose or torn stair carpet
row.visual_description: Carpet on stairs is bunched, torn, or not tacked down flush to each step edge.
detection_cues: visible carpet lip or wrinkle at step edge
carpet pulling away from stair nose
recommended_fix: Remove loose carpet or tack/re-secure it tightly to every step
row.post_op_modifier: A snagging carpet edge can trip a walker user whose gait and balance are already impaired post-op.
row.citation: Carpet on the stairs must be tight to every step; remove it or tack it down if it is loose or torn.

row.name: Missing grab bar at tub/shower
row.visual_description: No grab bar visible on wall inside tub or shower enclosure.
detection_cues: no anchored bar near tub entry
only tile or glass surfaces to grab
recommended_fix: Install ADA-height grab bar inside tub/shower
row.post_op_modifier: Walker user must pivot and bear weight on operated hip during tub transfer without support, greatly raising fall/dislocation risk.
row.citation: Grab bars should be installed inside the tub or shower and beside the toilet to help you get in, out, up and down.

row.name: Missing grab bar at toilet
row.visual_description: No grab bar mounted on wall adjacent to toilet.
detection_cues: toilet paper holder only fixture nearby
no bar within arm's reach of toilet
row.post_op_modifier: Sitting/standing from toilet stresses hip flexion limits; lack of bar forces unsafe unsupported motion for walker user.
row.citation: Grab bars should be installed inside the tub or shower and beside the toilet to help you get in, out, up and down.

row.name: Slippery tub/shower floor
row.visual_description: Tub or shower floor bare and glossy with no non-slip mat or adhesive safety strips visible.
recommended_fix: Add non-slip mat or adhesive safety strips
row.post_op_modifier: Wet slick surface combined with reduced single-leg stance post-surgery sharply raises fall risk.
row.citation: The floor of the tub or shower needs a non-slip mat or adhesive safety strips.

row.name: Loose or curled bath rug
row.visual_description: Small bath rug on floor without non-skid backing, showing curled edges or slid out of position.
recommended_fix: Remove rug or replace with non-skid backed rug
row.post_op_modifier: Walker feet catch easily on loose rug edges, high trip risk while weight-bearing is restricted.
row.citation: Small bath rugs that slide or have curled edges should be removed, or replaced with rugs that have a non-skid backing.

row.name: No night light on path to bathroom
row.visual_description: Hallway or bathroom path dark at night with no visible night light or low-level illumination source.
recommended_fix: Install night light along bed-to-bathroom path
row.post_op_modifier: Nighttime bathroom trips are common post-op; poor visibility with a walker raises fall risk when patient is least alert.
row.citation: Keep a night light on so the path to the bathroom is visible at night.

row.name: Missing raised toilet seat or safety frame
row.visual_description: Standard-height toilet with no raised seat attachment or safety frame visible around it.
detection_cues: toilet seat at standard low height
no frame with armrests around toilet
recommended_fix: Add raised toilet seat or toilet safety frame
row.post_op_modifier: Low seat forces excessive hip flexion beyond post-surgical precautions, risking dislocation for walker user.
row.citation: A raised toilet seat or a toilet safety frame makes it easier to sit and stand, especially after hip surgery.

plan.prompt: a pair of sneakers left on the stair tread, casting a soft shadow, matching the warm indoor lighting

a small bath rug lying on the tile floor with curled, upturned edges and no non-skid backing visible, slightly askew as if slid out of position, casting a soft shadow consistent with the room's lighting

scene.judge_note: A single shoe is placed on a stair tread midway up the staircase, creating a trip/fall hazard.

scene.name: Loose or curled bath rug
scene.judge_note: No bath rug added; instead the tub now shows claw feet, an unrelated change.
